Using RAG with SurveyDokum

Source: vignettes/using-rag.Rmd
using-rag.Rmd

What this guide covers

SurveyDokum’s LLM-based documentation (sd_document(), sd_generate_roxygen()) writes from the statistics computed by sd_summarise() alone, by default. RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) lets you additionally feed the model background material you choose yourself – a survey methodology glossary, a controlled vocabulary, previous codebooks used as style examples, a bilingual terminology list – so its writing draws on more than the numbers and its own general knowledge.

RAG support in SurveyDokum is a deliberately thin, optional layer: SurveyDokum does not build, ship, or maintain a knowledge store for you. It only consumes one you build yourself with the ragnar package, from whatever reference material you choose – your own survey methodology documentation, controlled vocabularies, previous codebooks, style guides, glossaries, or anything else ragnar can turn into text. This guide walks through building such a store with ragnar from scratch, then connecting it to SurveyDokum’s own functions, in general terms that apply regardless of what material you bring.

As a concrete example, this guide was developed against a small prototype store built from a handful of European Social Survey (ESS) documentation PDFs and a couple of reference web pages – the pitfalls noted along the way are ones actually hit while building that prototype, not hypothetical ones, and they apply the same way whatever your own source material happens to be.

This vignette is a parallel English-language translation of the package’s Finnish vignette (“RAGin käyttö SurveyDokumin kanssa”) – there is also a Swedish version (“Använda RAG med SurveyDokum”). All three cover the same workflow.

Prerequisites 

install.packages("ragnar")     # CRAN; brings in the duckdb dependency
install.packages("pdftools")   # fallback for reading PDFs, see Step 1
install.packages("rvest")      # fallback for reading web pages, see Step 1

ragnar needs an embedding model to turn text chunks into vectors. Since SurveyDokum already relies on a local Ollama installation for sd_document()/sd_generate_roxygen(), this guide uses an Ollama embedding model too, keeping the whole pipeline offline – relevant when your reference material is sensitive (e.g. restricted-access microdata documentation):

ollama pull embeddinggemma:300m

Any other Ollama embedding model works too – just use its name in embed_ollama() in Step 3 below. Make sure the Ollama server is running (default address http://localhost:11434).

Step 1: Read your source documents into Markdown

ragnar’s own read_as_markdown() uses MarkItDown, which downloads its own Python environment (via uv) on first use, and preserves heading structure the best of the options here. In practice it can fail on Windows with an error such as "Error loading Python module _ragnartools.markitdown" – most likely Windows or antivirus software blocking a downloaded native library (e.g. onnxruntime). If you hit this, two fallbacks avoid the Python environment entirely, at the cost of raw text without heading structure:

library(ragnar)

# PDFs, via pdftools:
read_pdf_fallback <- function(path) {
  pages <- pdftools::pdf_text(path)
  txt <- paste(pages, collapse = "\n\n---\n\n")
  MarkdownDocument(txt, origin = path)
}

# Web pages, via rvest:
read_html_fallback <- function(url) {
  page <- rvest::read_html(url)
  main_node <- rvest::html_element(page, "main")
  if (length(main_node) == 0 || is.na(main_node)) main_node <- page
  txt <- rvest::html_text2(main_node)
  MarkdownDocument(txt, origin = url)
}

Use whichever route works on your machine:

pdf_files <- list.files("path/to/reference_pdfs", pattern = "\\.pdf$", full.names = TRUE)
markdown_docs <- lapply(pdf_files, read_pdf_fallback)   # or read_as_markdown()
names(markdown_docs) <- basename(pdf_files)

Step 2: Clean up repeated headers, footers and page numbers (PDFs only)

pdftools::pdf_text() returns raw page text, including running headers/footers (e.g. a document title repeated on every page) and page-number lines – these become noise in your chunks if left in. A helper that removes lines which repeat across most pages (rather than searching for specific text, so it works for any PDF) is worth writing once and reusing:

strip_repeated_headers_footers <- function(pages, n_lines = 2, threshold = 0.5, prefix_len = 30) {
  split_pages <- strsplit(pages, "\n")
  n <- length(split_pages)

  get_candidates <- function(lines) {
    lines <- trimws(lines)
    lines <- lines[lines != ""]
    if (length(lines) == 0) return(character())
    unique(c(utils::head(lines, n_lines), utils::tail(lines, n_lines)))
  }
  candidate_lines <- unlist(lapply(split_pages, get_candidates))

  # Case A: the whole line repeats identically (short IDs, page numbers)
  line_counts <- table(candidate_lines)
  repeated_lines <- names(line_counts[line_counts >= threshold * n])

  # Case B: only the line's PREFIX repeats, while the rest varies by section
  # (e.g. "Annual Report 2024 -- Methodology  Chapter 3")
  prefixes <- substr(candidate_lines, 1, prefix_len)
  prefixes <- prefixes[nchar(trimws(prefixes)) >= 10]
  prefix_counts <- table(prefixes)
  repeated_prefixes <- names(prefix_counts[prefix_counts >= threshold * n])

  vapply(split_pages, function(lines) {
    trimmed <- trimws(lines)
    keep <- !trimmed %in% repeated_lines
    if (length(repeated_prefixes) > 0) {
      keep <- keep & !(substr(trimmed, 1, prefix_len) %in% repeated_prefixes)
    }
    keep <- keep & !grepl("^(page\\s*)?[0-9]{1,4}(\\s*(/|of)\\s*[0-9]{1,4})?$", trimmed, ignore.case = TRUE)
    paste(lines[keep], collapse = "\n")
  }, character(1))
}

Apply it before wrapping the text in MarkdownDocument(), i.e. inside read_pdf_fallback() above: pages <- strip_repeated_headers_footers(pages).

Step 3: Chunk and build the store 

store_path <- file.path("path/to", "my_reference.ragnar.duckdb")

store <- ragnar_store_create(
  location = store_path,
  embed = embed_ollama(model = "embeddinggemma:300m"),
  overwrite = TRUE,
  title = "My reference material"
)

for (doc_name in names(markdown_docs)) {
  chunks <- markdown_chunk(markdown_docs[[doc_name]])
  ragnar_store_insert(store, chunks)
}

ragnar_store_build_index(store)

Two pitfalls worth knowing about before you hit them:

  • Insert each document’s chunks separately, as a fresh markdown_chunk() result. A version-2 store (the current default) adds heading context to each chunk’s text automatically during insert. If you combine chunks from several documents into one data.frame first (e.g. with do.call(rbind, ...)) before calling ragnar_store_insert(), that automatic step breaks with "modifying chunks$text is not supported with store@version == 2". Loop over documents and insert as you go, as above.
  • ragnar_store_build_index() must run before ragnar_retrieve() works at all. Without it, retrieval fails with an error naming DuckDB’s BM25 function (match_bm25 does not exist) – the index is what makes that full-text search possible, so it is not optional, and it needs to run again after any batch of new inserts.

Give store_path as an absolute path, not a relative one – if your working directory happens to be some other project when you first build the store, that is where the .duckdb file will land.

Once built, a store on disk should be connected to, not rebuilt, on later runs:

if (file.exists(store_path)) {
  store <- ragnar_store_connect(store_path)
} else {
  # ... build as above ...
}

Rebuild (overwrite = TRUE) only when you change the embedding model or add documents you want indexed from scratch.

Step 4: Try retrieval directly 

hits <- ragnar_retrieve(store, "your query here", top_k = 5)

# ragnar_retrieve() returns a tibble whose text column gets truncated when printed --
# use a small helper to see the full text of each hit:
print_ragnar_hits <- function(hits) {
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(hits))) {
    row <- hits[i, ]
    cat(sprintf("--- hit %d/%d: %s (chars %s-%s) ---\n",
                i, nrow(hits), basename(row$origin), row$start, row$end))
    cat(row$text, "\n\n")
  }
}
print_ragnar_hits(hits)

(In the ESS-based prototype, a query like “How is political trust measured?” reliably surfaced the right codebook and questionnaire chunks – what works well for you will depend entirely on what you’ve indexed.)

ragnar_retrieve() combines vector search with DuckDB’s BM25 full-text search. Worth knowing if you mix conceptually different kinds of material in one store (e.g. survey microdata documentation alongside an abstract metadata standard): BM25 will surface matches on shared vocabulary (e.g. “codebook”, “variable”, “documentation”) even between documents that aren’t actually about the same thing. This is a property of hybrid search, not a bug to clean up – it is exactly what happened, for example, when mixing ESS survey documentation with DDI Alliance standard pages in the prototype. If it becomes a problem, keeping “content” and “reference standard” material in separate stores, or filtering retrieved chunks by their origin, are both options; SurveyDokum does not do either of these for you.

Step 5: Connect the store to SurveyDokum

Once you have a working store, SurveyDokum’s own functions pick it up via the store argument – everything from here on is a thin retrieval step in front of the prompt SurveyDokum was already building:

library(SurveyDokum)

store <- ragnar_store_connect(store_path)
data <- sd_read("survey_data.csv")

# Retrieval alone, for inspection -- one query per variable, using its name and label:
context <- sd_retrieve_context(data, store, top_k = 2)
cat(context)

# Used automatically by the documentation functions:
sd_document(data, model = "gemma3:12b", store = store)
sd_generate_roxygen(data, "survey_data", store = store)

store defaults to NULL everywhere in SurveyDokum, which skips retrieval entirely – every example in the “Getting started” vignette that does not mention store behaves exactly as before this feature existed. top_k (default 2) controls how many chunks are retrieved per variable; sd_retrieve_context()’s max_chars (default 600) truncates each retrieved chunk before it is inserted into the prompt, so a handful of long reference entries can’t dominate it.

If a query fails against the store (e.g. it is unreachable, or the embedding model is not running), sd_retrieve_context() turns that into a warning rather than an error and simply omits that variable’s background material – an unavailable reference store never blocks documentation from being generated.

Summary – all commands in sequence 

library(ragnar)
library(SurveyDokum)

# 1.-2. Read documents and clean PDF noise
pdf_files <- list.files("path/to/reference_pdfs", pattern = "\\.pdf$", full.names = TRUE)
markdown_docs <- lapply(pdf_files, read_pdf_fallback)
names(markdown_docs) <- basename(pdf_files)

# 3. Chunk and build the store (once)
store_path <- file.path("path/to", "my_reference.ragnar.duckdb")
store <- ragnar_store_create(
  location = store_path,
  embed = embed_ollama(model = "embeddinggemma:300m"),
  overwrite = TRUE
)
for (doc_name in names(markdown_docs)) {
  ragnar_store_insert(store, markdown_chunk(markdown_docs[[doc_name]]))
}
ragnar_store_build_index(store)

# On later runs, just connect:
store <- ragnar_store_connect(store_path)

# 4. Try it
print_ragnar_hits(ragnar_retrieve(store, "your query here", top_k = 5))

# 5. Use it with SurveyDokum
data <- sd_read("survey_data.csv")
sd_document(data, model = "gemma3:12b", store = store)
sd_generate_roxygen(data, "survey_data", store = store)
